reasons: Compliant finding: the cited pricing/revenue-share paragraphs set fixed, redacted fee and revenue-share amounts with no benchmarking or matching obligation against third-party terms, so nothing obliges Corio (the licensee/customer) to extend best terms to Commerce One.
Party roles are correctly identified — Corio pays the fees and is our party; Commerce One is the vendor — and the rule only bites where the Customer must give the Vendor no-less-favourable terms.

Consistent with a compliant status, no redline was rendered (redline text is identical to the original) and no counterparty comment was proposed, which is the expected output for an internal evidence finding.

Deterministic checks are empty and the negative-search rationale (no hits for 'most favored', 'no less favorable', 'best pricing', 'preferential', etc.) is a reasonable basis for the preferred-position classification; there is also no Vendor-granted MFN to preserve.
